Catharina Ziekenhuis (Eindhoven)
Imaging Department
Date: 15 Jan 2025
Exam: mpMRI Prostate

Clinical indication: Rising PSA (8.4 ng/mL) with suspicious DRE. Prior negative biopsy in 2023. Evaluation for prostate cancer.

FINDINGS:
The prostate volume measures 45.02 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a focal, ill-defined hypointense lesion within the peripheral zone of the mid left prostate, measuring approximately 12 mm in its greatest dimension. This lesion exhibits restricted diffusion on high b-value DWI (b=1400) with corresponding hyperintensity on the ADC map. Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) sequences show early, focal enhancement corresponding to the DWI abnormality. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified. The central gland shows benign prostatic hyperplasia without focal suspicious lesions. No suspicious lymphadenopathy or osseous metastases are visualized.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 4 lesion in the peripheral zone, mid left prostate.

previous_notes.text: Patient presented for baseline screening. PSA measured at 0.8 ng/mL. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. Discussed risk factors and surveillance strategy. Biopsy performed at this time showed no malignancy.

pathology_report:
Biopsy timepoint 1 (2023): The submitted tissue cores were reviewed and showed no evidence of malignancy. No cribriform or intraductal patterns were identified. Perineural invasion was absent.

Biopsy timepoint 2 (2025): Histological examination reveals acinar adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 3+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 2. No cribriform or intraductal patterns were identified. Perineural invasion is absent. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, mid left.

Summary: There is histological progression from a negative biopsy to ISUP grade group 2 disease.

AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology): Timepoint 1 — grade group 1; Timepoint 2 — grade group 3.
